bugs: Cycle detection walks every node reachable from the new task's deps on every add, so cost is O(V+E) per add and quadratic when building large graphs (a performance issue, not a correctness bug)
emit() queues a closure that snapshots the listener set at delivery time, not at emit time, so a listener subscribed between queueing and flush receives an event that predates its subscription
dependentsOf entries for ids that are never added stay forever (minor)
strengths: Phase is a discriminated union carrying per-state data (the attempt, the backoff handle, the terminal value or error), so invalid combinations cannot be represented
A single isCurrent(task, attempt) identity check covers late settles, timeouts and cancels
Binary heap with lazy invalidation: an entry is live only while it is the task's current queued phase object
Transactions with a queued event flush guarantee the documented event order under re-entrancy
An exceptionally thorough black-box test suite with exact event-sequence assertions, re-entrancy and hygiene checks (no global timers or Date.now), plus a mutation-testing script
weaknesses: Everything is in one ~500-line file, with no separate modules for the heap or the emitter
The deferred event delivery is subtle: a nested call returns before its own events reach listeners, which needs care to reason about
The order of duplicate check versus validation differs from common expectations (documented, though)

bugs: ctx.deps is built with deps[dep] = ..., so a dependency id of "__proto__" sets the object's prototype instead of creating an own key
findCycle is recursive and copies the path at each step ([...path, node]), so deep chains can overflow the stack and long paths cost O(n^2)
dispatch() scans the whole queued Set linearly for every start, giving O(n^2) total dispatch on large queues
strengths: The attempt-token pattern cleanly ignores stale settles
Handles an abort listener re-entrantly cancelling during attemptFailed
Good NOTES covering open decisions, including the onIdle-mid-operation subtlety
weaknesses: A flat Task record with many optional, mutually dependent fields (controller, timers, token, value, error) leaves state invariants implicit
Cascade sets state, but result rejection happens in two places (finish and cascade), which is easy to get wrong when extending
Thin test suite: few exact event-order assertions, no unhandled-rejection checks, no hygiene checks for global timers or Date.now
TimeoutError is added as the cause of a timeout, an extra type of debatable value

bugs: timeoutMs: Infinity is rejected with a RangeError, which is stricter than the brief implies (documented, but may surprise callers)
NOTES points to an external spec.md (redacted path) for the full decision record, which is not in the repo
The cascade cause is the first dead dependency in deps order rather than the edge the cascade actually traversed; documented, but it differs from a 'direct path' reading
strengths: Clean modular split: a generic Heap and Emitter in src/internal, and the scheduler logic in index.ts
Unmet-dependency counters plus a forwardRefs map make readiness O(1) per edge
Cycle detection runs only when a forward reference to the new id exists (or a self-dependency), so it is O(deps) in the common case; it is iterative
Iterative graph walks, with a 20k-deep chain test proving there is no stack exhaustion
'Commit then emit' discipline, so listeners always observe final states
Tests install an unhandled-rejection guard per file and include a 300-task randomized priority check
weaknesses: Some tests assert loosely (log.map(e => e[0])) rather than exact payloads
No test of global timer or Date.now avoidance
The assignDependencyError stack walk is clever but harder to follow than a BFS-carried cause

result.rationale: X and Z are both high-quality, well-reasoned designs. Z is the better-factored and more scalable implementation (heap and emitter modules, unmet counters, cheap and iterative cycle detection). X wins overall on the strength of its exemplary black-box test suite with mutation testing, its precise documentation, and the elegant phase-union and attempt-identity invariants. Y is correct and readable, but it scales poorly (linear dispatch scan, recursive path-copying cycle search) and has a __proto__ ctx.deps bug. Y's tests are also noticeably thinner and less precise than the other two.
